**Recurrence.** Squaring the recurrence gives a_{n+1}² − 5a_n a_{n+1} + a_n² = 1. Subtracting the same identity at index n−1 and dividing by a_{n+1} − a_{n−1} gives a_{n+1} = 5a_n − a_{n−1}. The division is valid because the sequence is strictly increasing. The first terms are 5, 24, 115, 551, ….

**Telescoping.** Dividing the identity by a_n a_{n+1} gives 1/(a_n a_{n+1}) = r_n + 1/r_n − 5, where r_n = a_{n+1}/a_n. The linear recurrence gives r_n − 5 = −1/r_{n−1}. So 1/(a_n a_{n+1}) = 1/r_n − 1/r_{n−1}, and the sum telescopes to 1/r_N − 1/r_0. Here r_0 = 5 (with a_0 = 1), which is consistent with r_1 = 24/5 = 5 − 1/5. As N → ∞, 1/r_N → 1/α = β = (5 − √21)/2. The sum is therefore β − 1/5 = (23 − 5√21)/10.
